scope: Solana transaction delivery, routers, venues and trading terminals
method: Official protocol/vendor documentation reviewed where accessible. Product claims are not independent benchmarks; no credentials or live transaction paths used.

discoveries: Listed as Solana transaction delivery/landing infrastructure.
Publicly stated performance requires independent, region-matched measurement.
patterns: Separate submission acknowledgement from confirmation and finality.
Measure landing slot, expiry, fees and retry behavior per route.
overlap: Potential transport adapter only; no signing authority should move to provider.
risks: Endpoint behavior, fees and availability unverified.
Fast submission can increase duplicate/retry costs.
validation: Verify current API and terms.
Run isolated non-capital tests and reconcile confirmed signatures.

provenance: Astralane official quickstart and public docs; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Docs describe transaction submission through relay/staked paths, tips and configurable retry behavior.
Public provider/client materials describe silent drops under rate limits, so transport success cannot equal landing.
patterns: Persist send intent, provider receipt, signature status and confirmed outcome separately.
Calculate tips and priority fees in realized cost.
overlap: Transport provider could fit behind existing execution authority; signer remains local and policy-controlled.
risks: Provider retries/tips can cause duplicate cost or overpay.
API key and endpoint limits must remain secret and bounded.
validation: Verify current endpoint and fee semantics.
Test rate limiting, timeout, duplicate submission and on-chain confirmation using authorized tests.

provenance: Official provider website entry; exact public API contract not established in this pass.
discoveries: Listed as Solana trading/execution infrastructure.
Supported paths, pricing and telemetry require direct official documentation review.
patterns: Maintain per-route delivery, cost and confirmation metrics.
Treat provider labels as metadata, not authorization.
overlap: Potential delivery route; no code integration approved.
risks: Claims and availability not independently verified.
Unknown fee/retry semantics.
validation: Obtain official API docs and current terms.
Test submission idempotency, landing and cost on isolated transactions.

provenance: Official Ironforge product website entry; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Listed as Solana network infrastructure/service provider.
Specific RPC/stream products, regions and service terms need product-level verification.
patterns: Track provider and region alongside slot lag and error rate.
Fail over only with gap detection and source reconciliation.
overlap: Possible infrastructure provider; existing RPC abstraction should remain the integration seam.
risks: Capabilities and SLAs unverified.
Provider failover can create inconsistent observations.
validation: Verify API docs, limits and archive range.
Inject outage/failover and duplicate-source cases.

provenance: Jupiter official product site; developer API reviewed separately in SRC-220.
discoveries: Jupiter is a Solana swap and portfolio interface that routes across liquidity venues.
A UI route is not itself a stable integration contract.
patterns: Use direct API quote/build contracts for integrations, with route freshness and simulation.
Verify token mint and output amount before signing.
overlap: Core swap router context; integration documentation is tracked in separate source record.
risks: UI prices and available liquidity can move before execution.
Route/program support changes over time.
validation: Validate exact API version and confirmed output.
Test transaction versioning and fee accounting.

discoveries: Portfolio UI aggregates wallet holdings and activity for user review.
Displayed portfolio valuation is not a canonical realized-PnL ledger.
patterns: Use portfolio views as an independent reconciliation aid.
Account for fees, failed transactions, transfers and open positions in internal ledger.
overlap: User-facing portfolio context; do not duplicate as accounting authority.
risks: Indexing delays and token pricing gaps can distort balances.
Wallet/portfolio connection has privacy implications.
validation: Compare sampled balances and signatures to RPC and internal fills.
Keep realized and unrealized PnL distinct.

provenance: Current official Jupiter Order & Execute documentation, accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: The current recommended Meta-Aggregator flow is GET /swap/v2/order followed by signed POST /execute; /order without taker returns a quote and does not assemble a transaction.
Order responses report router, fee mint and transaction version; current docs permit requesting v1 only as a supported-version ceiling, while actual v1 support depends on route and order mode.

The local Terminal research adapter now omits taker and rejects transaction payloads; SYLPH runtime execution still uses a separate manual /build adapter and the pinned web3.js path does not decode or sign v1.
patterns: Separate no-taker quote research from transaction construction and signing.
Bind any future execution response to router, request ID, transaction version, fee mint and finalized wallet deltas.
Keep API version migrations behind deterministic mocked-contract tests.
overlap: Primary candidate swap adapter using existing bridge and authorization.
risks: Changing from manual /build to /order + /execute would move landing and confirmation behavior to Jupiter and alter execution authority boundaries.
Jupiter documents v1 transaction output for a subset of Meta-Aggregator routes; the current web3.js decoder cannot sign that version.
Fees are token-denominated and route-specific; quote output is not the final wallet delta.
validation: Test no-taker quote response and reject any transaction field.
For future execution, pin official response fixtures for v0/v1, router variants, expiries and fee-mint accounting.
Keep signing, submitting and realized settlement in their existing separately authorized pipeline.
sources.license: API terms and rate limits require review

provenance: Official Pump.fun bonding curve documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Official docs describe a virtual-reserve bonding curve and automatic atomic migration to PumpSwap at graduation.
Docs state buys/sells move price along the curve and trading fees apply; fee schedule must be read at execution time.
patterns: Represent bonding-curve and graduated AMM as distinct market states.
Calculate size-aware executable price and lifecycle transition from on-chain state.
overlap: Venue lifecycle extends existing market/execution bridge.
risks: Stale curve state creates price-impact errors.
Migration and fee details can change; third-party labels may lag.
validation: Use official program IDs/SDK and captured pre/post-graduation fixtures.
Simulate buy/sell at multiple sizes and reconcile actual net amounts.
sources.license: Protocol docs; program terms/version require review

provenance: Official PumpPortal website/docs entry; prior catalog notes indicate metered trade streams and distinct Local/Lightning APIs; current details not independently revalidated in this pass.
discoveries: Third-party Pump.fun integration offers event feeds and transaction construction/submission products.
Local transaction construction and hosted-wallet submission have materially different custody boundaries.
patterns: Prefer locally controlled signing with transaction inspection where supported.
Record per-call fee, protocol fee, network fee and returned transaction signature.
overlap: Potential launch-event provider and execution transport; avoid making it a canonical feed or signer.
risks: Pricing, metering and API behavior can change.
Hosted-wallet modes may transfer custody/signing authority.
validation: Recheck current fee schedule/docs and terms.
Use only local-signing route in isolated tests; verify transaction bytes before signing.

provenance: Official Raydium product/docs entry; detailed SDK source reviewed in earlier repository batch.
discoveries: Raydium provides Solana AMM and launch/pool infrastructure.
Pool type and program lifecycle determine quote and account decoding semantics.
patterns: Key market state by mint plus pool address and program/version.
Use pool-specific quote math and on-chain simulation.
overlap: Venue integration belongs in existing AMM bridge.
risks: Multiple pool designs and migration paths.
Indexers may lag pool creation or liquidity changes.
validation: Test supported pool types against official SDK fixtures and RPC state.
Measure full fill and fees on simulation/test environment.
sources.license: Protocol/product docs; SDK-specific terms reviewed separately

provenance: Official Meteora site and DBC developer guide; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Meteora offers launch and AMM products including Dynamic Bonding Curve and DAMM lifecycle.
DBC migration targets DAMM v2 according to official guide; not every token uses this path.
patterns: Track launch mechanism and migration state per pool.
Implement lifecycle-specific decoders and fee models.
overlap: Adds supported venue lifecycle in existing bridge.
risks: Protocol account layouts and fee rules are versioned.
Transfer-hook behavior may alter actual transfer amounts.
validation: Use official SDK/docs and versioned account fixtures.
Compare quote to simulated and confirmed output.

provenance: Official Orca website; Whirlpools source/docs reviewed in earlier batch.
discoveries: Orca provides concentrated-liquidity Whirlpool markets and swap interface.
Liquidity distribution across ticks affects price impact and executable depth.
patterns: Quote against current tick arrays and pool state, not headline TVL alone.
Track price impact across position size and route.
overlap: Venue-specific implementation fits existing AMM bridge.
risks: Tick-array/account state can change between quote and landing.
Program version and token extensions affect compatibility.
validation: Test tick crossings and partial liquidity using official SDK fixtures.
Simulate and reconcile realized output/fees.
sources.license: Protocol docs; SDK terms review required

discoveries: Trading/research platform advertises token discovery, wallet tracking and execution features.
Signals and wallet rankings are provider-derived and do not prove realized performance.
patterns: Use wallet signals as candidates for on-chain verification, with source timestamp.
Separate copy-trade analytics from independently calculated net PnL.
overlap: Research interface only unless a documented API contract is independently evaluated.
risks: Ranking may omit related wallets, transfers, fees and unrealized losses.
Automated copying can create latency, slippage and custody risks.
validation: Reconstruct selected wallets from on-chain transfers and fills.
Do not automate execution from unverified platform signals.

discoveries: Trading terminal presents Solana token discovery and manual execution features.
UI speed and displayed token data are not independently verified execution guarantees.
patterns: Use terminal displays as analyst workflow, then verify mint, pool and transaction on-chain.
Record actual fills and fees outside UI display.
overlap: Manual trading surface only; no engine integration established.
risks: UI/extension phishing and stale quotes.
Wallet signing requires transaction inspection and scoped hot-wallet funding.
validation: Verify domain and transaction details before wallet approval.
Reconcile signatures and token balance changes.

provenance: Official Trojan site and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Product offers Telegram and web terminal trading workflows with automation/order features.
User-facing terminal capability does not define a public integration API or guarantee fills.
patterns: Keep manual terminal use distinct from bot execution controls.
Verify exact transaction and custody path before wallet approval.
overlap: No direct engine API integration established.
risks: Telegram bot and wallet permissions introduce custody/security risk.
Displayed order status may differ from finalized chain state.
validation: Read official security/custody docs and test with isolated wallet only.
Verify every transaction via signature and confirmed account delta.
